theme.title: Rotation: Value/Defensives → Growth
theme.summary: Financials (+1.54%) and Consumer Discretionary (+1.22%) led the market today, while Materials (-1.13%) and Energy (-0.83%) brought up the rear. Growth sectors outpaced the rest, averaging +1.17% versus +0.24% for defensives and +0.31% for value, consistent with risk appetite favoring higher-beta names. Major indices moved in a tighter band — S&P 500 +1.06%, Dow +1.18%, Nasdaq +1.40% — without one clearly dominating. Small caps underperformed as well, with the Russell 2000 at +0.51%, hinting the move favored large, established balance sheets over smaller, more rate-sensitive companies. The VIX fell 5.98% to 14.32, which reads as an orderly rotation rather than panic-driven selling. Gold added 0.97% to $4,520.50, crude oil was little changed at $91.74, and bitcoin gained 4.94% — cross-asset moves weren't all pointing the same direction as equities.
